stories.title: Aiims Delhi performs India's first open fetal surgery to repair spinal defect in unborn baby - Firstpost
Robotic knee surgery shows improved one-year outcomes
stories.summary: Patients receiving robotic-assisted knee replacements reported superior functional outcomes and less pain at one year compared to those treated with conventional techniques, according to a quasi-randomised trial in Germany. The study compared an advanced four-dimensional alignment workflow against a standard femur-first mechanical procedure in 845 patients.

stories.title: Triplet therapy tested for older AML patients
stories.summary: A phase I/II trial evaluated a triplet regimen of venetoclax, quizartinib, and chemotherapy in older patients with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia ineligible for intensive induction. The VEN-A-QUI study enrolled 75 patients across 12 Spanish centers to determine the recommended dose and assess clinical activity in high-risk populations.

stories.title: Experimental Vaccine for Pancreatic Cancer Could Help Find and Destroy Lurking Cancer Cells - Discover Magazine
ADC therapy shows high response in breast cancer trial
stories.summary: The investigational antibody-drug conjugate SHR-A1811 produced an 81.5 percent objective response rate in patients with HER2-low invasive breast cancer. The single-arm HELEN-015 trial in China evaluated the compound as a monotherapy to shrink tumors and lymph nodes before patients underwent definitive surgical intervention.

stories.title: CAR T-cell therapy linked to lupus symptom reduction
stories.summary: Research presented at the American College of Rheumatology meeting indicates that CAR T-cell therapy is associated with consistent reductions in disease activity for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. The findings were shared during the ACR Convergence 2026 event held in Orlando, Florida.

stories.title: Early results for azer-cel in multiple sclerosis
stories.summary: A phase 1 trial of the allogeneic CAR T-cell therapy azer-cel reported no high-grade toxicities and stable or improved disability scores in patients with progressive multiple sclerosis. The study provided early evidence of immune reset and B-cell depletion in the first clinical evaluation of the treatment.

stories.title: Ranking tracks China's growing biotech sector
stories.summary: STAT and WireScreen published a list of China's 25 most valuable publicly traded biotech firms to track the industry's varying strategies. The report suggests the sector is not a monolith but a collection of companies with diverging ambitions amid a domestic scientific renaissance and ongoing geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Amino acid change improves influenza B vaccine
stories.summary: Researchers in Beijing found that a single D212N amino acid substitution in the hemagglutinin protein of an influenza B vaccine candidate broadens protective capacity in mice. The study suggests this minimal modification addresses limitations in current seasonal vaccines that lack specific glycosylation motifs for cross-neutralizing antibody responses.

stories.title: Thiamine Deficiency Re-Emerges Among Pregnant, Lactating Women In Parts Of Northeast: ICMR-NIN Study - NDTV
Centre proposes restricting treatment packages to government hospitals
stories.summary: The National Health Authority has proposed reserving 112 treatment packages under the Ayushman Bharat scheme exclusively for government hospitals starting December 1. The move would limit beneficiaries from accessing these specific procedures at empanelled private hospitals, adding to 23 packages already restricted to the public sector.

stories.title: India reports 38 percent drop in TB mortality
stories.summary: India achieved a 38 percent decrease in tuberculosis mortality rates since 2015, surpassing the global average reduction of 35 percent, according to the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026. The country also recorded a 94 percent treatment success rate for patients during the same period.

stories.title: ICMR study finds thiamine deficiency in pregnant women
stories.summary: An ICMR-NIN study found suboptimal vitamin B1 levels in 20.1 percent of pregnant and lactating women surveyed in Assam and Tripura. Published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, the research examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and dietary factors in the region.

stories.title: Public health group calls for TB reporting transparency
stories.summary: Following the release of the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, the Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India network flagged the country's continuing high disease burden. While mortality has declined, India still accounts for approximately one-fourth of global TB cases and 23 percent of global TB deaths.

stories.title: Health spending triples as out-of-pocket costs fall
stories.summary: Union government health expenditure rose to 4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24, up from 1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14. National Health Accounts estimates show the share of out-of-pocket spending by households fell from 64.2 percent to 42.7 percent over the same decade, reflecting a shift in healthcare financing.

stories.title: ICMR begins palliative care feasibility study
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has launched a multi-state implementation research study to improve coverage of palliative care. The project serves as a feasibility study for a potential national policy, as the country currently lacks a dedicated framework for comprehensive care for serious illness.

stories.title: Diabetes spike linked to traditional Kashmiri feasts
stories.summary: Experts suggest the Kashmiri wazwan, a multi-course meal that can reach 5,500 calories, is a key factor in the region's rising diabetes cases. A book released on World Diabetes Day noted that these festival feasts provide several times the average daily caloric requirement for an individual.

stories.title: Outdoor workers report health issues as Delhi air quality worsens
stories.summary: As Delhi's Air Quality Index crossed 400, outdoor workers including traffic police and gig workers reported breathing difficulties, persistent coughs, and burning eyes. Many employees continue to work without adequate protection, as staying indoors is not an option for those in roadside or field-based roles.

stories.title: Measles cases rise as vaccination rates fall
stories.summary: Endemic measles poses a danger to the unvaccinated, including infants and those with weakened immune systems. Former CDC official Walter Orenstein noted that infection can occur in public spaces like supermarkets. At least four infants too young for vaccination have died from the virus this year.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in Congo reaches record scale
stories.summary: Six months after the WHO declared a public health emergency, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded 11,254 cases and 5,505 deaths. It is now the second-largest epidemic on record, driven by structural conditions and ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: Health Ministry reports thousands of doctor resignations
stories.summary: Between 2024 and 2026, 4,126 medical specialists and officers resigned from the Health Ministry. The government appointed 23,911 new officers during the same period, while 2,298 were gazetted as specialists. Private sector employment remains the primary reason cited for the departures.

stories.title: U.S. loses measles-elimination status
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the U.S. measles-elimination status, ending a designation held since 2000. The decision follows reports of continuous virus circulation for over a year. The U.S. has recorded more cases in the last 18 months than in the preceding decades.

stories.title: NHS to end Palantir contract in 2029
stories.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care will extend its contract with Palantir for two years, delaying the end of the partnership until 2029. The software firm provides the federated data platform for the NHS. Ministers intend to use the time to transition to British providers.

Congo Ebola response falters
stories.summary: Six months into the current Ebola outbreak, containment efforts remain inadequate. Government data shows over 11,000 cases and a death rate approaching 50 percent. Experts suggest there is little chance of bringing the epidemic under control within the next year.

stories.title: India Eradicated Polio 15 Years Ago, Pakistan Still Struggles To Eliminate Virus: Report - NDTV
U.S. measles-free status revoked after 26 years
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organization has revoked the U.S. measles-elimination status due to continuous transmission of the virus. The country is currently experiencing its highest case count in over three decades, with 7,500 infections and 13 deaths reported.

stories.title: Goyal calls for healthtech collaboration
stories.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal has urged Indian and Egyptian startups to collaborate on affordable diagnostic tools and medical devices. The proposal aims to foster cross-border investments and partnerships to develop technologies suitable for expansion into wider regional markets.

Prosper AI named to digital health list
stories.summary: CB Insights included Prosper AI in its 2026 Digital Health 50 list. The company describes itself as an AI workforce that turns patient demand into practice growth. Analysts noted that the selected startups are finding new ways to extend clinicians' reach and simplify patient access to treatment.

stories.title: Apple and OpenEvidence launch health chat study
stories.summary: Apple and OpenEvidence have launched an experimental artificial intelligence study in Las Vegas. The project is designed to explore the application of AI in a healthcare context. The companies have not provided further details on the specific clinical goals of the research.

stories.title: Study links cannabis addiction to suicidal thoughts
stories.summary: A study of 415,000 Americans found that adults with cannabis use disorder face 57 percent higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts. The risk is particularly elevated among women and younger adults. Researchers are examining these effects as marijuana availability and social acceptance continue to increase.

stories.title: Family finances determine access to mental health care
stories.summary: Monash University research of 5.4 million Australians shows that family finances are increasingly determining who receives timely psychological treatment. Despite seeking medical assistance, disadvantaged children face the greatest barriers to care. The divide between wealthy and low-income families is preventing thousands from receiving necessary mental health support.

stories.title: Pink noise suggested as conversational tool
stories.summary: Dartmouth researchers have identified a conversational recipe they call pink noise to help people navigate difficult discussions. Published in Science Advances, the study suggests this approach may help individuals return to more enjoyable and engaging interactions. The researchers did not specify if it works on the internet.

stories.title: Rural Connecticut reports lowest mental health readiness
stories.summary: Rural communities in Connecticut report the lowest perceived readiness for mental health promotion compared to suburban and urban areas. An analysis of statewide survey data published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems highlights these disparities. Public health challenges remain critical, particularly among the youth population.

stories.title: Review links fruit and vegetable intake to lower depression risk
stories.summary: A review of observational research published in the Journal of Affective Disorders suggests that eating more fruits and vegetables is linked to a lower risk of developing depression. Mental health professionals are increasingly examining daily nutrition as a potential way to help reduce the risk of mood disorders.

stories.title: Weekly park visits linked to child development
stories.summary: Children who visit parks at least once a week show better social-emotional development than those who visit less frequently, according to a study from the Universities of Exeter and Bristol. Researchers suggest that outdoor play is a simple way to support a child's emotional wellbeing and social skills.

stories.title: Study examines link between pets and child mental health
stories.summary: As households increasingly consider the benefits of animal companionship, a study in Spain has explored the emotional bonds between children and their pets. The research investigates whether getting a pet provides the expected mental health advantages for developing children. The emotional bond is known as attachment.

stories.title: Regular park visits show measurable impact on child mental health
stories.summary: A new study suggests that regular visits to local parks have a measurable impact on child mental health. Researchers found that outdoor play supports social and emotional development, which provides the foundation for good mental health throughout childhood and adolescence. The findings address concerns regarding sedentary lifestyles.

stories.title: Study finds 1 in 5 children with diabetes face mental health challenges
stories.summary: A PGI study of 97 children with Type 1 Diabetes found that 20 percent experience significant psychological maladjustment. Published in the Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism, the research notes that depression is strongly linked to long-term blood sugar averages. The remaining children matched local healthy population norms.

research.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
research.summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia. Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.

research.title: Daily Quiz: Communication with extraterrestrial intelligence
research.summary: From a radio telescope in Puerto Rico to a distant globular cluster, explore the science, symbolism and audacious ambition behind humanity’s 1974 attempt to communicate with extraterrestrial intelligence. Daily Quiz: Communication with extraterrestrial intelligence

research.title: MIT scientists discover a surprising way to boost the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
research.summary: MIT scientists discovered that carefully timed bursts of gentle pink noise during sleep can strengthen the brain’s natural cleaning waves, which help flush away potentially harmful waste. The breakthrough could pave the way for new treatments aimed at improving sleep and memory while potentially reducing the buildup of.

research.title: New wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
research.summary: A revolutionary new wearable patch could help people get more restorative sleep without medication or surgery. Developed by University of Texas researchers, the device uses gentle ultrasound to stimulate deep brain regions, helping participants enter REM sleep 43 minutes faster and remain there 16 minutes longer on average.

research.title: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that the heart ages unevenly, with surprising hotspots of inflammation and scarring concentrated in the valves and major blood vessels rather than the heart muscle. The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about cardiac aging and could help researchers develop new ways to protect the heart as.

research.title: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder
research.summary: Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that this common vitamin could inspire new treatments.
